data.gender_notes: Orphanna is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Greek goddess of fertility and childbirth
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Orphana was a goddess of fertility and childbirth. Her name is derived from the Greek word 'orphan', meaning 'child'. In Christian tradition, the name Orphana is sometimes used as a variant of the name Orpheus, the mythological figure who traveled to the underworld to save his beloved Eurydice. However, there is no clear biblical or saintly association with the name Orphana.
data.etymology: Orphanna belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Greek goddess of fertility and childbirth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Orphanna total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Orphana, derived from the Greek mythological figure, may evoke intrigue and interest due to its mythological origins. It may also symbolize connection to the rich history of Greek mythology and the importance of fertility and childbirth in ancient cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Orphana may hold spiritual significance as a reminder of the power and reach of divine love. The name Orpheus, linked to Orphana in mythology, is known for his ability to charm even the ruler of the underworld with his music and love for Eurydice. Similarly, Orphana may remind us of the power and depth of love to move even the most unmovable hearts, connecting us to something greater than ourselves and inspiring us to live fully and lovingly.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Orphanna: The sorrowful mother, bearing the grief of losing her child, yet holding on to faith and hope in God's plan for redemption.

historical_references.reference: Orphanna was a legendary figure in medieval Scotland, known as the 'Queen of the Fairies'. She was believed to protect children and was often invoked during childbirth and childhood illnesses. According to folklore, she was a fairy queen who had once been a beautiful human princess who was transformed into a fairy after being falsely accused of witchcraft.

Another reference to Orphanna can be found in the 'Orphic Hymns', a collection of ancient Greek religious texts. In one of these hymns, Orphanna is referred to as the 'Goddess of the Ways and the Crossroads'. She was believed to be a deity who could guide travelers on their journeys and protect them from harm.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Orphanna' is a modern derivative of the word 'orphan.' In the current context, it is associated with initiatives supporting orphanages, adoption, and philanthropy. On Instagram, users might share pictures and stories from their visits to orphanages or use the hashtag #Orphanna to raise awareness about adoption. TikTok creators often produce content centered around their experiences with adoption or share educational resources about the topic. On YouTube, channels dedicated to adoption and supporting orphanages create videos that showcase personal stories, resources, and advice for those considering adoption. The overall trend is one of compassion, advocacy, and community building around the theme of caring for orphans and children in need.
